question: Our data contains 7 predictors. How many different models (i.e. combinations of predictors) does best subset selection have to evaluate?

answers.feedback: Correct! There are 2^7 = 128 possible subsets. mlxtend skips the empty model without any predictors, so it actually fits 127 of them.
Correct! There are 2^7 = 128 possible subsets, and 127 of them contain at least one predictor.
Not quite. Each predictor can either be in the model or not, so there are 2 × 2 × ... × 2 = 2^p combinations.
